title: A Software Bug Burned $440 Million in 45 Minutes #shorts
description:
On August 1, 2012, Knight Capital, one of Wall Street's biggest traders, switched on new software. One forgotten server woke up old code and lost $440 million in 45 minutes.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
first_comment: Who's more to blame: the engineer who missed one server, or the bosses with no kill switch? 👇

lines.text: In twenty twelve, one firm lost four hundred and forty million dollars in forty-five minutes.
No hacker. No rogue trader. Just one forgotten server.
Knight Capital was one of America's biggest stock traders.
Days earlier, engineers installed new software on eight servers.
But on one server, the update never arrived.
Instead, it woke up old code, dead for years.
At the opening bell, it started buying and selling like crazy.
Four million trades, in one hundred and fifty-four stocks.
Every minute, it lost about ten million dollars.
And nobody knew how to stop it.
When they finally shut it down, four hundred and forty million dollars were gone.
Knight's stock fell about seventy-five percent in two days.
It needed an emergency rescue, and within a year it was sold.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
